objects.maker: Domaine de la Romanée-Conti (the de Villaine and Roch families)
objects.made: the Abbey of Saint-Vivant held the vineyard from 1232; named for the Prince of Conti, who bought it in 1760; the domaine dates from 1869
objects.count: 1.8 ha monopole; about 450 cases a year; about 600 bottles in 1945

record.what: a bottle of the 1945 from Robert Drouhin’s cellar

objects.t: The Prince of Conti outbid Madame de Pompadour for this 1.8-hectare vineyard in 1760, and Wikipedia gives its average price as US$21,336 a bottle. Only about 600 bottles were made in 1945, the last vintage before the old vines were pulled up. Two of Robert Drouhin’s sold at Sotheby’s New York in October 2018 for US$558,000 and US$496,000 against an estimate of US$22,000–32,000; another of his bottles made US$812,500 at Acker in March 2026. The reports do not say whether these prices include the premium.
src: CNBC, Bottle of wine sells for record-breaking $558,000 (2018)
Forbes Australia, 1945 French wine sells for US$812,500 (2026)
Vinetur, 1945 DRC sells for $812,500 in New York (2026)

objects.n: La Tâche, Domaine de la Romanée-Conti
objects.made: named by the de Croonembourg family in 1631; the domaine’s since the Liger-Belair auction of 1933
objects.count: 6.06 ha monopole; about 1,870 cases a year

record.what: a 5.5-litre bottle (the report gives both 1971 and 1972)

objects.t: La Tâche is the domaine’s second monopole, more than three times the size of Romanée-Conti. It came to the domaine after the Liger-Belair vineyards were auctioned in 1933, and in 1932 most of Les Gaudichots was merged into it. A 5.5-litre bottle made US$150,000 at Bonhams in June 2024, the house’s highest price for a single bottle.
src: The Drinks Business, Bonhams sells rare bottle of La Tâche for US$150,000 (2024)

objects.made: first recorded in 1837; Madame Loubat’s from 1925 to 1961; the Moueix family’s since
objects.count: about 11.4 ha on a clay island; about 95% Merlot
objects.t: Pétrus grows almost all Merlot on a clay outcrop on the high terrace of Pomerol. Jean-Pierre Moueix became its sole agent in 1943 and took it to America in 1945; Christian Moueix made it from 1970. In 2021 Christie’s offered by private sale a bottle of the 2000 that had spent 14 months on the International Space Station.
src: Decanter, Pétrus wine: behind the legend
Christie’s press release via Auction Daily, space-aged Pétrus 2000 (2021)

objects.count: three bottles sent from the château’s own cellar in 2010

record.what: one of three bottles of the 1869

objects.t: Three bottles of the 1869 came straight from the château’s cellar to a Sotheby’s sale in Hong Kong in October 2010. Each made HK$1.815 million, which Decanter gave as US$233,972. Every one of the 284 lots went to Asian buyers; the reports do not say whether the price includes the premium.
src: Decanter, Lafite prices spiral at record Sotheby’s Hong Kong auction (2010)
The Drinks Business, Lafite auction blasts prices skyward (2010)

objects.count: a celebrated vintage; cases of twelve bottles and of six magnums reach the sale room

record.what: a case of six magnums of the 1945

objects.t: Mouton’s 1945 is the vintage of the end of the Second World War. At Christie’s first evening wine sale in Beverly Hills in 2006 a twelve-bottle case made US$290,000 and minutes later a case of six magnums made US$345,000, each a record for a case at the time. Both went to anonymous bidders.
src: Decanter, Mouton 45 shatters world record twice (2006)

objects.maker: Screaming Eagle (founded by Jean Phillips; Stan Kroenke sole owner since 2009)
objects.count: about 500 cases a year from 57 acres

now.n: bought by Chase Bailey of Incline Village, Nevada

objects.t: Jean Phillips, a former estate agent, founded the cult Napa Cabernet in 1986, and it still makes only about 500 cases a year. At the charity Napa Valley Wine Auction of 4 June 2000 a six-litre bottle of the 1992 made US$500,000, then a world record for a single bottle. Banks and Kroenke bought the winery in 2006 and Kroenke has owned it alone since 2009.
src: Napa Valley Vintners, 20th Napa Valley Wine Auction sets world records (2000)
VinePair, 8 things you should know about Screaming Eagle

objects.count: three or four barrels; about 35 (Decanter) to 40 (Langton’s) bottles survive

record.cur: A$; the source gives no US$ figure

objects.t: Max Schubert made the first Grange in 1951, and when the Penfolds board rejected it he gave most of the bottles away. About 35 to 40 survive, most of them in complete sets of Grange. In July 2021 one made A$142,131 at Langton’s, which Decanter gave as about US$104,587; in December 2021 another made A$157,624 with the 16.5% premium, a record for a bottle of Australian wine.
src: Endeavour Group (Langton’s), New world record set for a single bottle of Penfolds Grange 1951 (2021)
Decanter, Penfolds Grange 1951 sets new auction record (2021)

objects.made: the estate since 2005; the 2015 vintage released in 2019
objects.count: 550 bottles of the 2015, of which 240 were released
objects.t: Loïc Pasquet makes Liber Pater from ungrafted vines and forgotten Bordeaux grape varieties at Landiras in the Graves. The 2015 was released at €30,000 a bottle, about US$33,420 at the time, making it the most expensive new release in the world. Only 550 bottles were made.
src: Decanter, Liber Pater to release world’s most expensive wine (2019)

objects.count: his cellar: 1,064 bottles (855 bottles, 209 magnums) in 215 lots

record.cur: US$m hammer as reported by Wine Spectator

objects.t: Henri Jayer, who died in 2006 aged 84, made Cros Parantoux in Vosne-Romanée from 1978 to 2001. His last cellar sold at Baghera/wines in Geneva in June 2018 for CHF 34.5 million (Wine Spectator: US$34.7 million with a 20% premium). The top lot, fifteen magnums of Cros Parantoux from 1978 to 2001, made CHF 1,164,000; Wine Spectator gives US$1,171,217.
src: Euronews, Last batch of Henri Jayer wine sells for €30m (2018)
Wine Spectator, Henri Jayer’s personal cellar shatters wine auction record (2018)

objects.maker: Massandra winery (founded by Prince Lev Golitsyn under Nicholas II)
objects.made: since 1894; the oldest bottle a 1775 sherry
objects.count: about 500,000 bottles (TASS) to a million (Wikipedia) in tunnels over 3 km long

now.n: Massandra’s cellars, Crimea (annexed by Russia in 2014)

objects.t: Massandra was built in the 1890s as the tsar’s showcase winery for the Crimean palaces, and its cellars hold one of the largest old-wine libraries anywhere. The oldest bottle is a sherry of 1775; one sold in 2001 for £32,000, and the winery later said it would ask at least €1 million for another. Sotheby’s first offered Massandra wines in the West in 1990.
src: Jancis Robinson, Massandra: Crimea’s liquid crown jewels
TASS, Crimea winery puts ‘oldest wine bottle’ on offer

objects.maker: The Macallan distillery; label by Valerio Adami
objects.made: distilled 1926; sixty years in sherry casks; bottled 1986
objects.count: 40 bottles of the 1926; 12 with Adami’s label

record.what: a bottle of the 1926 with the Adami label

objects.t: The Macallan filled the cask in 1926 and bottled it sixty years later in 1986; only 40 bottles exist, and twelve carry a label designed by the Italian artist Valerio Adami. One made £2.1875 million at Sotheby’s London in November 2023, which Whisky Advocate gives as US$2,724,908 with the 25% premium. It is the most expensive bottle of any wine or spirit sold at auction.
src: Whisky Advocate, Macallan bottle sells for $2.7 million (2023)
Euronews, Rare Scotch whisky becomes world’s most expensive bottle (2023)

objects.made: from casks filled in 1960 (Mizunara oak) and 1964 (white oak); released June 2020
objects.t: Suntory’s oldest release joined whisky from a Mizunara cask of 1960 and a white-oak cask of 1964, and only 100 bottles were released in June 2020. Two months later one made HK$6.2 million, about US$795,000, at Bonhams Hong Kong against an estimate of HK$580,000–780,000. It was then the auction record for Japanese whisky.
src: Bonhams press release via Auction Daily, new world auction record for a bottle of Japanese whisky (2020)
Artdaily, New world auction record for a bottle of Japanese whisky set at Bonhams (2020)

record.what: the ‘Grand Frère’, largest of the three bottles

now.n: the ‘Petite Sœur’ is shown at Maison Gautier in Cognac country

objects.t: Three bottles of the 1762 survived in one family, reputedly brought home from the Cognac region in the 1870s by a foster son paid in bottles rather than wages. The largest made £118,580, about US$144,525, in Sotheby’s online sale of May 2020 against an estimate of £80,000–160,000, and went to a collector in Asia. The ‘Petit Frère’ sold in New York in 2014 for £48,000; the ‘Petite Sœur’ is in the Gautier museum.
src: Sotheby’s press release, one of only three remaining bottles of Gautier Cognac 1762 (2020)
Decanter, Oldest Cognac from 1762 fetches nearly $150,000 (2020)

objects.made: 2019, for the Only Watch charity auction
objects.count: one: the only Grandmaster Chime in steel, engraved ‘The Only One’
objects.t: Patek Philippe made one Grandmaster Chime in steel for the 2019 Only Watch sale, a reversible watch of 20 complications with five chiming functions. It made CHF 31 million, about US$31.19 million, at the Geneva charity auction run by Christie’s on 9 November 2019, the highest price paid for any watch. The proceeds went to research into Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
src: Wikipedia, List of most expensive watches sold at auction

objects.maker: Patek Philippe, for the banker Henry Graves Jr.
objects.count: one pocket watch, no. 198.385, with 24 complications
objects.t: Henry Graves Jr. paid CHF 60,000 for a gold pocket watch with 24 functions, among them Westminster chimes and a chart of the night sky over New York. It was shown at the Time Museum in Rockford, Illinois, sold at Sotheby’s in 1999 for US$11,002,500, and again in Geneva in 2014 for CHF 23,237,000, about US$24 million. The buyer in 2014 was anonymous.
src: Wikipedia, Patek Philippe Henry Graves Supercomplication
Wikipedia, List of most expensive watches sold at auction

objects.count: one: Newman’s own watch, engraved ‘Drive Carefully Me’
objects.t: Joanne Woodward gave her husband this Daytona with ‘Drive Carefully Me’ engraved on the back. James Cox, a friend of the family, owned it when Phillips sold it in New York on 26 October 2017 for US$17.75 million to an anonymous telephone bidder. Part of the proceeds went to the Nell Newman Foundation.
src: National Jeweler, Selling for $17.8M, Paul Newman’s Rolex sets record (2017)
Wikipedia, List of most expensive watches sold at auction

objects.maker: Abraham-Louis Breguet; finished by his son Louis-Antoine
objects.made: commissioned 1783; finished after Breguet’s death in 1823
objects.place: Museum for Islamic Art (L. A. Mayer), Jerusalem
objects.t: An admirer of Marie Antoinette, said to be Axel von Fersen, ordered from Breguet in 1783 a watch with a perpetual calendar, minute repeater, chronograph and automatic winding; it was finished only after Breguet died in 1823, thirty years after the queen. Sir David Lionel Salomons bought it in the 1920s and it went to the L. A. Mayer museum in Jerusalem, from which it was stolen in April 1983 with 105 other timepieces. It was traced to the thief’s widow and returned in 2007–08; it was valued at US$30 million in 2013.
src: Watchonista, The Breguet Marie-Antoinette and horology’s most notorious heist

objects.n: Patek Philippe Ref. 1518 in stainless steel
objects.t: A stainless-steel Ref. 1518 made in 1943 sold for US$11.14 million at Phillips in Geneva in November 2016. It ranks fourth among watches sold at auction, after the Grandmaster Chime, the Graves Supercomplication and Paul Newman’s Daytona.
src: Wikipedia, List of most expensive watches sold at auction

objects.maker: Rolex; owned by Bảo Đại, last emperor of Vietnam
objects.t: The Ref. 6062 of 1952 that belonged to Bảo Đại, the last emperor of Vietnam, made US$5.06 million at Phillips in Geneva in May 2017. Five months later Paul Newman’s Daytona made more than three times as much.
src: Wikipedia, List of most expensive watches sold at auction

objects.t: Breguet & Fils of Paris made pocket watch No. 2667 in 1814. It made US$4.69 million at Christie’s Geneva in May 2012, the highest price in the list for a watch made before 1900.
src: Wikipedia, List of most expensive watches sold at auction

objects.count: two prototypes; one sold, one kept by the company

now.n: the other coupé stays at the Mercedes-Benz Museum, Stuttgart

objects.t: The Mercedes-Benz racing department built two coupé prototypes of the 300 SLR in 1955. Mercedes sold one at a private auction in its Stuttgart museum on 5 May 2022 for €135 million, about US$143 million, a record for any car sold at auction. The buyer is a private collector; the proceeds fund a Mercedes-Benz Fund of scholarships in environmental science.
src: RM Sotheby’s press release, the 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé is sold for €135,000,000 (2022)
Wikipedia, List of most expensive cars sold at auction

objects.t: Ferrari built only 36 of the 250 GTO between 1962 and 1964, a front-engined 3-litre V12 for GT racing. One made US$48.4 million at RM Sotheby’s in Monterey in August 2018, and the 1962 car raced as a 330 LM made US$51.7 million in New York in November 2023. Many change hands privately.
src: Ferrari, The most celebrated car ever made
Wikipedia, List of most expensive cars sold at auction

objects.t: Juan Manuel Fangio and Stirling Moss drove the streamlined W 196 R; four complete ones are known and none had been offered for private ownership before. Chassis 00009/54 made €51,155,000 at RM Sotheby’s in the Stuttgart museum on 1 February 2025, which Hagerty gives as about US$53.0 million. It is the second-highest price paid for a car at auction.
src: Hagerty, $53M Mercedes-Benz W196 R is the second-most expensive car sold at auction (2025)
Wikipedia, List of most expensive cars sold at auction

objects.t: Bugatti built one La Voiture Noire in Molsheim for its 110th anniversary, an 8-litre, 16-cylinder, 1,500 PS coupé that reinterprets Jean Bugatti’s Type 57 SC Atlantic. The original black Atlantic it honours vanished before the German invasion of Alsace and has never been found. The new car was sold to an unnamed enthusiast for €11 million before tax.
src: Bugatti press release, La Voiture Noire: a one-off car for the anniversary (2019)

objects.t: A 1964 Shelby Daytona made US$42.9 million at Gooding Christie’s in Monterey in August 2026, the highest price in that list for an American car.
src: Wikipedia, List of most expensive cars sold at auction

objects.t: A 1956 Aston Martin DBR1 made US$22.55 million at RM Sotheby’s in Monterey in August 2017, the highest price in that list for a British car.
src: Wikipedia, List of most expensive cars sold at auction

objects.maker: mined by De Beers; cut from a 132.5-carat rough
objects.count: 59.60 carats, Fancy Vivid Pink, internally flawless

now.n: Chow Tai Fook, Hong Kong; renamed the CTF Pink Star

objects.t: De Beers mined the rough in Africa in 1999, and was cut into a 59.60-carat Fancy Vivid Pink, internally flawless. It first sold in 2013 for US$83 million to a cutter who defaulted; at Sotheby’s Hong Kong in April 2017 the chairman of the jeweller Chow Tai Fook bought it by telephone for US$71.2 million and renamed it in honour of his late father.
src: NPR, Pink Star diamond sells for $71 million, smashing auction record (2017)

objects.maker: from the collection of Sir Philip Oppenheimer of the De Beers diamond syndicate
objects.t: The 14.62-carat blue belonged to Sir Philip Oppenheimer, who controlled the diamond syndicate in London and headed the Central Selling Organisation. Christie’s sold it in Geneva in May 2016 for CHF 56.83 million, about US$57.5 million with the premium, to an anonymous telephone bidder; it was the most expensive jewel sold at auction until the Pink Star a year later.
src: National Jeweler, Oppenheimer Blue sells for record-setting $57.5M (2016)

objects.maker: probably from the Kollur mine, Golconda; recut for Louis XIV and again in London
objects.made: sold to Louis XIV in 1668 by Jean-Baptiste Tavernier
objects.place: National Museum of Natural History, Washington
objects.count: 45.52 carats, deep blue; the largest known blue diamond

now.n: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, Washington, since 1958

objects.t: Tavernier brought a blue of almost 115 carats out of India and sold it to Louis XIV, who had it cut as the French Blue; it was stolen in 1792 and surfaced in London in 1812, recut, and took the name of Henry Philip Hope. Harry Winston bought it from Evalyn Walsh McLean’s estate in 1949 and sent it to the Smithsonian by registered mail on 10 November 1958, at a cost of US$145.29. It draws millions of visitors a year.
src: Smithsonian Magazine, How the king of diamonds gave the National Museum of Natural History its crown jewel (2025)
Smithsonian NMNH Geogallery, The Hope Diamond (G3551)

objects.maker: Indian; recut by Garrard of London in 1852
objects.made: first recorded in the 14th–17th centuries (accounts differ)

now.n: the Crown of Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother, Tower of London

objects.t: The Mountain of Light passed from the Delhi sultans or the Mughals to Nadir Shah, who took it from Delhi in 1739, then to the Durranis of Afghanistan and to Ranjit Singh of the Punjab. The British took it when they annexed the Punjab in 1849, and it was recut from about 191 to 105.6 carats in 1852. It has been in the Queen Mother’s crown since 1937; India has repeatedly asked for its return.
src: Historic Royal Palaces, The Crown Jewels

objects.maker: found by Frederick Wells at the Premier Mine; cut by Joseph Asscher & Co., Amsterdam
objects.place: Jewel House, Tower of London (found at Cullinan, Transvaal)
objects.count: 3,106 carats rough; nine major stones and 96 small brilliants; Cullinan I 530.2 carats

now.n: Cullinan I in the Sovereign’s Sceptre with Cross and Cullinan II in the Imperial State Crown, Tower of London

objects.t: The largest gem-quality rough diamond ever found, 3,106 carats, came out of the Premier Mine in the Transvaal in 1905, and the colony’s government bought it for £150,000 as a gift to Edward VII. Asscher’s of Amsterdam split it in 1908 into nine major stones; the two largest, Cullinan I and II, are set in the sceptre and the Imperial State Crown. Cullinans III and IV were re-set in Queen Camilla’s crown for the coronation of 2023.
src: Historic Royal Palaces, The Crown Jewels

objects.made: found in the 17th century; set in the Imperial Sceptre, completed 1774

now.n: the Imperial Sceptre, Diamond Fund, Moscow Kremlin

objects.t: Count Grigory Orlov bought this Golconda diamond, reputedly for 1.4 million Dutch florins, and offered it to Catherine the Great in the hope of winning her back. She did not return to him, but she named the stone after him and had it set at the top of the Imperial Sceptre. It is shown in the Kremlin’s Diamond Fund.

objects.maker: Indian, by legend from the Kollur mine; sold by Thomas Pitt

now.n: the French crown jewels at the Louvre, on show since 1887

objects.t: Thomas Pitt sold the stone in 1717 to the regent Philippe d’Orléans for £135,000. It was set in Louis XV’s crown in 1722, stolen in 1792 and found in the roof timbers of a Paris attic, and Napoleon wore it in the guard of his sword. It has been shown at the Louvre since 1887.

objects.maker: a pearl from the Pearl Islands, Panama

record.cur: US$m with premium, reported as ‘over US$11 million’
record.what: La Peregrina, from Elizabeth Taylor’s collection

objects.t: La Peregrina was a Spanish crown jewel for more than two centuries, left Spain with Joseph Bonaparte and was bought from Napoleon III by the Marquess of Abercorn. Richard Burton paid US$37,000 for it at Sotheby’s in 1969 for Elizabeth Taylor. At the sale of her jewels at Christie’s New York in December 2011 it made over US$11 million against an estimate of US$3 million.

objects.count: one in private hands that may be lawfully owned; two in the Smithsonian

record.what: the only privately ownable 1933 Double Eagle

now.n: two other examples in the National Museum of American History, Washington

objects.t: The 1933 twenty-dollar gold pieces were struck but never issued: Roosevelt took the country off gold and in 1934 the Mint ordered them melted. A few escaped, and the government recovered all but this one, which after a legal battle with the Treasury is the only example a private person may lawfully own. Stuart Weitzman bought it in 2002 for US$7.59 million and sold it at Sotheby’s New York in June 2021 for US$18.9 million to an anonymous buyer, the most paid for any coin.
src: Smithsonian Magazine, 1933 Double Eagle sells for $18.9 million (2021)
Wikipedia, List of most expensive coins

objects.count: a handful in several varieties; the EB on breast is unique
objects.t: Ephraim Brasher struck these gold pieces privately from 1787, with the arms of New York on one side; each was worth sixteen Spanish dollars. The EB-on-wing example made US$9.36 million at Heritage in January 2021, the record for a gold coin at public auction. The unique EB-on-breast coin was sold privately in 2011 for nearly US$7.4 million.
src: Wikipedia, List of most expensive coins

objects.t: The 1794 dollar was the first silver dollar of the United States; 1,758 were struck and about 140 survive. This specimen, graded SP-66 and widely believed to be the first struck, sold at auction in 2013 for US$10,016,875 and in January 2022 the collector Bruce Morelan sold it to GreatCollections for US$12 million.
src: Greysheet, America’s first silver dollar acquired for $12 million by GreatCollections (2022)
Wikipedia, List of most expensive coins

objects.n: Edward III gold florin, the ‘double leopard’
objects.maker: the English royal mint under Edward III
objects.count: three known: two in the British Museum, one in a private collection

record.cur: GBP; the source gives no US$ figure
record.what: the third known florin, found in southern England

now.n: two found by the Tyne in 1857, British Museum

objects.t: Edward III’s first gold coin was valued at six shillings, more than its gold was worth, so merchants refused it and it was withdrawn within months, in August 1344. Only three survive: two found on the banks of the Tyne in 1857 are in the British Museum, and a third found in southern England in 2006 sold for £460,000, then a record for a British coin, and was sold to an American collector in 2016.

objects.n: 1804 silver dollar, the Sultan of Muscat specimen
objects.made: dated 1804; delivered in 1835 as a diplomatic gift
objects.count: this Proof-68 is the finest known

record.what: the Sultan of Muscat 1804 dollar, Proof-68

objects.t: This 1804 dollar was delivered in 1835 as a diplomatic gift to Said bin Sultan, Sultan of Muscat and Oman. It came to London in 1917, passed through the Watters, Brand, Childs and Pogue collections, and made US$7.68 million at Stack’s Bowers in August 2021, against US$4.14 million in 1999.
src: Artdaily, Stack’s Bowers sells finest known 1804 silver dollar for record $7.68 million (2021)

objects.made: soon after the Ides of March, 44 BC

record.what: the third known gold EID MAR

objects.t: Brutus struck the coin to celebrate the killing of Julius Caesar, with two daggers and the cap of liberty above the words EID MAR, the Ides of March. Only three are known in gold. This one made £3,240,000, about US$4.188 million with the premium, at Roma Numismatics in October 2020, the record for an ancient coin.
src: CoinWeek, NGC Ancients-certified EID MAR aureus realises nearly $4.2 million (2020)
Wikipedia, List of most expensive coins

objects.n: Gold dinar of the caliph Yazid II
objects.t: An Umayyad gold dinar struck in 723 made US$6,029,400 at Morton & Eden in April 2011; another made US$4.78 million there in October 2019. Both rank among the most expensive coins ever sold.

objects.n: Patek Philippe Star Caliber 2000, set of four

record.what: a set of four Star Caliber 2000 watches

objects.t: A set of four Star Caliber 2000 pocket watches made US$11.9 million at Sotheby’s in December 2025, the highest price on Sotheby’s own list of its most expensive watches.

objects.t: Audemars Piguet’s Grosse Pièce No. 16869 made US$7.7 million at Sotheby’s in December 2025, second on Sotheby’s list of its most expensive watches.
